items.headline: Copilot Vision lets you share your screen or point your camera and AI explains what it sees
items.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot Vision allows users to share their screen or point their phone camera at physical objects and documents. Copilot analyzes what it sees alongside work context and web data to explain issues, spot problems, and suggest next steps. This multimodal capability extends Copilot beyond text-based assistance into visual problem-solving.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's Microsoft Practice (150+ certified experts) and M365 deployments can immediately leverage Copilot Vision for client support scenarios — technicians photographing equipment for AI diagnosis, field teams sharing site conditions for real-time guidance, or finance teams scanning invoices for automated processing. Add this to AI Discovery Workshops as a concrete example of multimodal AI reducing response time. Relevant to Manufacturing (equipment troubleshooting), Financial Services (document processing), and Healthcare (visual record review) verticals.

items.headline: Agentforce Help Agent launches with pay-per-resolution pricing in July 2026
items.summary: Salesforce made Agentforce Help Agent and Agentforce Customer Service Portal generally available in July 2026. The Help Agent features pay-per-resolution pricing, charging only when the AI successfully resolves a customer issue. This shifts risk from the buyer to Salesforce and represents a major commercial model change for enterprise AI — customers pay for outcomes, not seat licenses or API calls.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift is a Salesforce Summit Partner and Agentforce Ready — this pricing shift changes how we scope ROI in Agentforce implementations. Our 150+ pre-built Agentforce agents can now be pitched with outcome-based pricing, reducing client financial risk and shortening sales cycles. Immediately update Agentforce proposals to reference pay-per-resolution as a differentiator vs fixed-cost chatbot platforms. Especially relevant to our Service Cloud clients in Technology, Healthcare, and Financial Services who operate high-volume support centers.

items.headline: Healthcare AI adoption reaches 70% with 85% of executives reporting revenue gains
items.summary: NVIDIA's 2026 State of AI Report shows healthcare AI adoption jumped to 70% from 63% year-over-year, with 85% of healthcare executives reporting revenue gains from AI deployments. Nearly half of organizations are planning 10%+ budget increases for AI. AI agents are now automating 89% of clinical documentation tasks with measurable efficiency improvements. This represents a shift from pilot programs to production-scale AI delivering P&L impact.

items.headline: Deloitte AI hallucination scandal costs $290K and sparks FINRA 2026 compliance crackdown
items.summary: Deloitte faced a $290,000 AI hallucination incident that triggered FINRA (Financial Industry Regulatory Authority) to issue its first dedicated generative AI compliance guidance in its 2026 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report. FINRA explicitly named hallucinations and bias as risks that financial services firms must manage before deploying AI. This marks the first time a major financial regulator has made AI governance a formal oversight priority.

items.headline: EU AI Act high-risk AI compliance deadline is August 2 2026 with fines up to EUR 35M or 7% revenue
items.summary: The EU AI Act's compliance deadline for high-risk AI systems is August 2, 2026 — 11 days away. Organizations deploying high-risk AI must have functioning risk management systems, data governance frameworks, technical documentation, and human oversight mechanisms in place and demonstrable before deployment. Non-compliance carries fines up to EUR 35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. Any AI processing personal data must comply with both the AI Act and GDPR simultaneously.
